V.rationale: Visa's fundamental health and trajectory are strong: revenue accelerated to +17.1% YoY ($11.23B Q2 2026), net income grew +31.5% YoY on real operating leverage, and structural margins remain elite (51.7% net, 61.1% operating). The franchise is wide-moat with dominant U.S. market share (61% of credit card spending) and multiple secular growth vectors (cash displacement, VAS at 30% of revenue growing 24%, stablecoin settlement at $7B annualized run rate). However, two factors temper conviction toward the +0.2 to +0.5 band rather than higher: (1) operating cash flow collapsed to $3.01B in Q2 2026, a 0.50x conversion ratio vs. net income — a genuine outlier that needs monitoring, and (2) valuation multiples (PE, P/B, EV/EBIT) are absent from the quantitative data pack, though web-sourced forward P/E of ~24x sits below the five-year median of 25.93x, suggesting the market has not fully priced in the reacceleration. The $20B buyback authorization (largest in company history) and near-term catalysts — World Cup spending tailwind ($11.1B projected), stablecoin platform talks with Stripe/Coinbase, and agentic commerce integration with OpenAI — provide credible re-rating paths. Score lands at +0.35: solidly attractive fundamentals with a below-median multiple and multiple dated catalysts, but tempered by the OCF quality flag and the inability to independently verify valuation from the data pack.
